title: Newborn rash — benign or concerning?
summary: Many newborn rashes are harmless and fade on their own. A few patterns need a look.
whatsNormal:
Several common rashes appear in the first days and weeks.

• Erythema toxicum — small red bumps with white centers, often day 2–5, fades in days
• Milia — tiny white bumps on nose and cheeks; not acne; resolves in weeks
• Heat rash — fine red dots in skin folds when baby is warm
• Diaper rash — red irritated skin in the diaper area; often improves with air time and barrier cream

Benign rashes usually do not bother the baby much and do not come with fever or poor feeding.
watchFor: Rash with fever in a baby under 3 months
Blisters, open sores, or honey-colored crusts
Rash that looks like bruises and does not fade when pressed
Spreading redness with warmth or swelling of surrounding skin
callDoctorIf: Rash with difficulty breathing, swelling of face, or vomiting
Purple or non-blanching spots (do not pale when you press)
Diaper rash with broken skin, pus, or no improvement in 2–3 days of home care
You are unsure — a photo for your pediatrician's nurse line is often enough to start
